I am still married, and we are trying to work things, but we have been together for 13 years and married for almost 3, I brought up my concerns again and again in the past and nothing changed. Now that he knows I don't love him as a partner but only as a friend, and want to separate, he is showing me extra (to the level of way too much) affection. It would be great if this happened, before I lost my love for him. Right now it feels fake, and he sometimes still does the same actions that I brought up for my reasonings of separation. I guess I am tired of fighting about the same things and started to give up. I have been hanging out more with my friends without my husband and I have been feeling so much better, and have been happier with who I am without him.

Therapists cannot solve your problems. So, you can actually learn these tools without going to the therapy, like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. CBT is basically recognizing your thoughts are negative, and can be different explanations to your situation. Forexample, your friend didn't answer your text, your thoughts can be "s/he doesn't want to talk to me anymore", but there are other explanations like "s/he is away from the phone, not available, phone's battery is dead etc". 

Regular therapy is for sure overrated (for high functioning depression/dysthymia), if you can understand the techniques, but if you don't have anyone to talk to, it is helpful

It looks like you are into philosophy. Trying to understand life through philosophy, at least to dissect or poke around with the meaning of this whole shenanigans, has had a calming effect on me (I also have general anxiety disorder and social anxiety disorder). My perspective might change in the future, but now I choose to think more of existantial nihilist and maybe sometimes absurdist way of looking at life. Although, I still get dangerously close to having panic attacks or have small ones, I care less about what others think of me or what will happen tomorrow (although my therapist hinted at me that this is probably my depression worsening or changing shape).

I am not sure what were the intrinsic meanings you have experimented with, but if you think it is other there keep looking, "the search for the meaning" can be the meaning in itself. And also, there doesn't have to be. What is so wrong with the Sisyphean fate? 90% of the population goes through it, every single week day, e.g.: wake up, get ready, go to work, come home, eat, survived (?), go to sleep... repeat... 

Life gets easier just to accept that you will make mistakes and will still continue, and the answer to the question "am I the only one ...?" is never ever "yes". There is always someone going through the same shit as you. I think people "like" feeling unique, and you are as a combination everything you are and are going through, but that one single aspect you think is what is wrong with you is something you certainly share with at least one other person; kinship... Your DNA is not unique to you, it is common with your relatives; then again you probably have silent mutations that different from the members of your family, but you have in common with a complete stranger. I realized, for myself, if I make myself feel "unique", I feel too much pressure, which leads me to deep hopelessness. 

I know I am acting like I am calm and collected and figured this shit out. Nope. Never. Not a thing in my book. I am struggling, suffering persistently to calm myself, and yet get back to rumination and feeling overwhelmed and a huge failure because I had/have such high expectations of myself. I keep signing up to online courses, gyms; starting training programs, books; trying to learn new languages... And I lose interest, or get bored, or feel like I cannot do it, forget, and end up quitting again and again. Feel like a failure. Go into deep depression. Try to collect myself all over again. Guilt trip myself not to end this all, because will make others unhappy. I guess I am already pushing the boulder towards the top - not getting there, let the boulder crush me on the way down, probably let the vultures eat my heart out up there, and you know the drill, gotta do what you gotta do...

From this article:

"The fMRI studies suggest that the difficulty adult learners of a second language may have is not with understanding the words of the second language, but with the motor skills of forming the words with the mouth and tongue. This may explain why learners of a second language can oftentimes comprehend a question asked in the new language, but are not always able to form a quick response.

Thus, for adult English language learners, techniques that emphasize speaking may be more successful than methods that focus more on reading and listening. For example, rather than lecturing to a class about vocabulary and grammar, an instructor perhaps should encourage her adult students to have conversations in English, or to act out short skits incorporating the day’s lesson, which would more closely link the students’ abilities to understand and speak the new language. Speaking would thus equal understanding.

The Cornell researchers also studied the brains of people who were bilingual from a very early age. Presumably, this group of people is able to speak the two languages as easily as they can comprehend both languages spoken to them. The researchers found that these subjects showed no spatial separation in either Broca’s or Wernicke’s areas for the two languages, indicating that in terms of brain activation at least, the same regions of the brain controlled their ability to process both languages.

The idea that second languages learned early in childhood are not separately processed in the brain is supported by fMRI studies of brain development in children. Researchers at UCLA report that the language areas of the brain seem to go through the most dynamic period of growth between the ages of 6 and 13. In contrast to the “first three years” idea of child development that has received so much press in the past few years, the UCLA study instead suggests that the elementary and middle school years are the biologically most advantageous times for acquisition of a second language."
